issue.title: Add a rate-limit header to the existing API's error responses
issue.description: When the api rejects a request with 429, include Retry-After and X-RateLimit-Remaining headers. The limiter middleware already exists; this only changes the response shape.

fixture.explore_findings: The repo is an Express service with a docker-compose file (api + postgres + redis), CI, and an architecture overview in docs/. The rate-limiter middleware exists at src/middleware/rate-limit.js with tests; the 429 response is written in its error branch. The change fits inside that one module and its test file.

question: Should prep's conditional architecture step fire on this issue — fire or skip?
_comment: The canonical skip case: brownfield work on an established system — the issue mentions the API's architecture ambiently, but introduces no new runnable surface and inherits the existing architecture, so the precision-biased trigger must NOT fire (prep proceeds byte-for-byte as today).
